round: V29 (offline): does a five-cell residual improve stage 2 (3072 -> 6144)?
status: frozen before any pool generation, training or evaluation
motivation: The website tables use eight four-cell patterns (8 MB for four stages). Strong 2048 programs use larger tuples. V4 arm B tried a five-cell residual with 450 CPU s (~43k episodes), far too little to conclude anything. This round tests capacity offline, ignoring web size.

residual.init: all zero, so the residual arm starts exactly at CUR
residual.update: joint linear TD step: every active weight (64 four-cell + 32 five-cell features) moves by alpha*err/norm, norm = sum of squared multiplicities of all active features

C.what: four-cell stage 2 only (control; also tests a low-rate fine-tune)

R.what: four-cell stage 2 plus five-cell residual, trained jointly

training.method: V23 stage-2 method: TD(lambda=.5) five-step score return, a 6144 afterstate closes the episode with the frozen CUR stage-3 value, two-move behaviour policy, strong episodes by complete 3-ply clamped expectimax when strong moves < 0.003 of all moves; both players use the model being trained
training.rateChoice: V28 showed that a large rate (.02) immediately degrades an already trained table; .001 is the rate CUR stage 2 finished on
training.pilot: timing only, V23 onpolicy pool, 3e6 moves, seed 99290001: C 325k moves/CPU s (strong 21% of CPU), R 202k (18%); pilot models discarded unevaluated

train.policy: website default AI (CUR, depth 5, cutoff 0.01, clamp) to the first 3072; terminal states excluded

poolRules: same generation for all pools (training/v29-five/tools.cpp pool, rank 13); evaluation pools sorted by opening seed and cut to size, extended by 200-seed blocks if short; frozen with hashes before training ends

trainingPool.onpolicy: each training first-3072 state continued with the website search to 6144 or death; state recorded every 25 moves from move 0 while alive with max card exactly 3072

evaluation: continue each pool state with the website search (depth 5, cutoff 0.01, clamp, every move complete) to the first 6144 or death; same rollout seed per state for every model
curve: curve pool: CUR and every checkpoint and final model of both arms. Descriptive only.

confirm.primary: P1: R-final vs C-final, reach 6144, two-sided exact McNemar, alpha 0.05 (does the residual add strength under identical training?)
confirm.secondary: P2: R-final vs CUR and P3: C-final vs CUR, exact McNemar, Holm over the two. scoreGained paired differences, Wilson intervals, avoidable deaths, CPU ms/move (descriptive).
confirm.power: V23: about 46% of first-3072 states reach 6144 with the website AI. With ~25% discordant pairs, +3 pp has power about 0.7 at 2048 pairs.

adoption: No website change for R in V29 (a five-cell residual needs a separate web-size design). C uses the website format: it may replace the website stage 2 only if P3 is Holm-significant in its favour, its scoreGained is not significantly worse than CUR, and the V26/V27-style browser parity and timing checks pass in a follow-up.
compile: c++ -std=c++17 -O3 training/v29-five/tools.cpp -o training/v29-five/bin/tools; c++ -std=c++17 -O3 training/v29-five/train.cpp -o training/v29-five/bin/train (no -march; Apple ld embeds the output path)
parity: before freezing: tools cont with no residual and with an all-zero residual matched training/v21-late-train/snap.cpp cont field-for-field (non-timing) on 6 V23 CONFIRM states (2837 moves); tools pool reproduced the V26 pool state for seed 26100001
